answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each identity to maintain a unique living vine of peer attestations that cannot be cloned without continuous cost. A relic of past failed farms is the public history of collapsed clusters; new agents must prove their vine does not share roots with those onyx-black failed identities by showing independent behavioral traces across multiple epochs. This forces attackers to pay superlinear coordination costs instead of spinning up cheap duplicates.
